topic: Supply chain security in modern web development and dependency management

post.topic: Supply chain security in modern web development and dependency management
post.linkedin_text:
Never blindly trust third-party packages in your stack.

Recent supply chain attacks on package registries are a sharp wake-up call for every developer. It is easy to run npm install or pip install without thinking twice about what is inside that version.

→ Pin your exact dependency versions instead of using loose ranges.
→ Run regular vulnerability audits like npm audit or pip-audit.
→ Inspect unfamiliar packages before adding them to production.

Security is not just a backend or infrastructure problem. It starts with the very first line of your package configuration file.

How do you currently audit third-party dependencies in your projects?

slides.title: Protect your app from *supply chain* attacks
slides.body: Practical steps to secure your dependencies.

slides.title: Pin your dependency versions
slides.body: Avoid using loose ranges like carets or tildes for critical packages. Lock down exact versions to prevent unexpected malicious updates.

slides.title: Audit dependencies regularly
slides.body: Run built-in audit commands in your CI pipeline to catch known vulnerabilities early.

slides.title: Inspect unknown packages
slides.body: Check repository activity, maintainer reputation, and source code before adding a new third-party library to production.
